prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported knee injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1273; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a rear-end collision in Pasadena, Texas, involving two vehicles traveling in the same lane of a city street. Driver 1 was stopped at a signal when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 struck the rear of Driver 1's car. Driver 2 stated that braking came too late to avoid contact, and Driver 1 gave a matching account of the sequence. Two witnesses at the scene described the impact the same way, and photographs taken at the location show rear-end damage on Driver 1's vehicle that fits the reported force of the collision. Driver 1 reported pain in the left knee, which struck the lower dash on impact, and that injury is consistent with a crash of this kind. Passenger, seated in the front right seat, was confirmed to be in the vehicle at the time. Officers found no sign of earlier damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as a named driver on the policy covering the vehicle involved. Both drivers were cooperative, exchanged information, and were transported no further than the scene.
